title: Woodshedding modern tunes after leaving Duke
summary: After years of only Duke's tunes he had to learn everyday songs, which gave him broader experience; now he will play any kind of music for money.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Well, when I left Duke's band I had to go and, we call it, woodshed tunes because I was playing nothing but Duke's tunes, you know, nothing but Duke. When I came out, well, I had to play what they were playing, the modern songs, I mean, you know, the everyday songs. So I had to woodshed that and it took me a long time, too. Altogether different.

But I'm sure glad because I've had the experience. It's given me a broader area to cover in music, like somebody would say, 'Would you play hillbilly?' Now I play any kind of billy for money. See, playing for kicks with me is over. I've had it.
You can still get kicks playing, can't you?
Oh, sure, but I mean -- but it's money time now, you know, because I'm getting kind of old now. Hold on.
